title: Summer and Kitchen
premise: Coral Okafor, a lighthouse keeper's grandson turned cautious novelist, returns to the coastal town of Saltmere for a family reunion he dreads, armed with a fake date arranged through a stranger's classified ad. The stranger turns out to be Juniper Vale, a visiting chef with a three-week contract and a past she's outrunning, and what begins as performance chemistry becomes dangerously real by the reunion's dessert course. As Coral's family pressures him to abandon writing for the family salvage business and Juniper's contract ends, both must decide whether love justifies the risk of being truly seen. In the end, Coral claims his identity as a writer at the reunion's closing dinner, and Juniper, having turned down a prestigious post abroad, opens a small restaurant in Saltmere where the two finally build a life measured in brave steps instead of safe ones.
about_author: Oscar Delacroix is the pen name of a former line cook who spent a decade writing love letters on the backs of order tickets before turning to fiction. He lives somewhere near the sea, where he insists all good romances are marinated.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Keeps Its Secrets
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral returns to Saltmere to help his grandmother prepare the Okafor family reunion, hiding his stalled novel and his dread of his father's expectations. Walking the lighthouse stairs at dusk, he admits he's spent twelve years shrinking. Emotional beat: quiet unease beneath nostalgia.

chapters.title: An Ad in the Back of Everything
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Desperate to survive the reunion without pitying relatives, Coral answers a classified ad offering 'fake dates, no questions.' The reply comes from someone named Juniper, who insists on one rule: total honesty about everything except each other. Emotional beat: wry hope.

chapters.title: Salt and First Impressions
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. They meet at the dockside café where Juniper works, and their rehearsed backstory collapses immediately—she's funnier, sharper, and more tired than her emails suggested. They improvise, and it works too well. Emotional beat: startled chemistry.

chapters.title: The Reunion Begins
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, brief Juniper interlude. Coral introduces Juniper to forty Okafor relatives; his father, Marcus, sizes up the stranger and dismisses Coral's 'little writing habit' within minutes. Juniper covers for Coral's silence with a story that lands. Emotional beat: humiliation softened by alliance.

chapters.title: What Juniper Is Running From
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper reveals her three-week contract at the café and the prestigious London post she fled after a public professional betrayal. She tells Coral the truth of her rule: honesty about everything except herself. Emotional beat: guarded vulnerability.

chapters.title: Dessert Changes Everything
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At the reunion's dessert course, Coral's aunt toasts the 'lovely couple,' and Juniper kisses Coral's cheek to sell it—but the kiss lingers a half-second too long. Both pull back, both pretend. Emotional beat: the fake becomes real.

chapters.title: Low Tide, High Honesty
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Walking the exposed flats at low tide, Coral confesses his abandoned novel and his fear that wanting a writing life means betraying his father's salvage business. Juniper listens without fixing him. Emotional beat: first real intimacy.

chapters.title: The Kitchen Test
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper invites Coral into the café kitchen to cook together; he's clumsy, she's exacting, and the banter burns hotter than the pans. She catches herself planning meals he'd like. Emotional beat: joy with an expiry date.

chapters.title: Marcus Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral's father offers him a partnership in the salvage company, framing it as legacy and duty—and a condition: give up the novel, the 'distraction,' the dream. Coral, terrified of losing his father again, doesn't say no. Emotional beat: the old cage, freshly painted.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, flashback-heavy. Coral recalls the accident that killed his mother twelve years ago, the novel he abandoned that night, and how invisibility became survival. Juniper reads the first three chapters without his permission. Emotional beat: grief unearthed.

chapters.title: The Rule Breaks
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper breaks her own rule and tells Coral about the betrayal in London—her business partner stealing her restaurant and her name. Coral holds her through the telling. They sleep apart but not honestly. Emotional beat: two people falling despite themselves.

chapters.title: One Week Left
chapters.summary: Dual POV. With Juniper's contract half gone, they stop pretending the timeline doesn't exist. They make a pact: no talk of after, only now. Both break the pact privately the same night. Emotional beat: sweetness sharpened by countdown.

chapters.title: The Grandmother Knows
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral's grandmother, the lighthouse keeper, tells him she watched him shrink for twelve years and that his mother would be furious about it—not about the novel, about the hiding. She gives him his mother's unfinished manuscript. Emotional beat: permission, finally granted.

chapters.title: Caught in the Middle of a Dinner
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At a family dinner, Marcus announces Coral's partnership publicly before Coral has agreed, and Juniper watches him freeze and accept. She says nothing, but her silence says everything. Emotional beat: the cost of small safe steps.

chapters.title: The Fight at the Café
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Juniper confronts Coral: she won't be the reason he shrinks, and he can't lend her pieces of himself while keeping the whole heart caged. She tells him her London offer has a deadline—she leaves in five days. Emotional beat: love and duty collide.

chapters.title: Five Days
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper drafts her acceptance to London and can't send it. She walks the lighthouse at night and finds Coral's mother's manuscript left on the stairs—Coral's way of showing her the story he never finished. Emotional beat: aching indecision.

chapters.title: The Salvage Dive
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral joins one last salvage dive with his father, and underwater, in the wreck his mother loved, he understands: duty without love is just drowning slowly. He surfaces and tells Marcus the truth. Emotional beat: the whole heart, risked.

chapters.title: The Reading at the Lighthouse
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral reads his mother's unfinished final chapter aloud to his grandmother and finishes it himself, in his own voice, for the first time in twelve years. He asks Juniper to hear the novel's ending—she's already at the door, suitcase packed. Emotional beat: climax of identity.

chapters.title: What Juniper Decided
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper turns down London, not for Coral, but because she finally admits Saltmere is the first place she's wanted to stay. She tells him at the dock, terrified, and he tells her the truth: the date was fake, the falling never was. Emotional beat: mutual surrender.

chapters.title: The Last Family Dinner
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At the reunion's closing dinner, Coral announces he's finishing the novel, declining the partnership, and staying in Saltmere. Marcus storms out; his grandmother raises a glass; Juniper caters dessert. Emotional beat: belonging claimed, cost acknowledged.

chapters.title: Summer and Kitchen
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Weeks later, Juniper signs a lease for a tiny restaurant called The Keeper's Table, and Coral finishes his novel in the lighthouse. They cook, they write, they argue about salt. Emotional beat: ordinary love, hard-won.

chapters.title: The Light Still Turns
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, epilogue. One year later, Coral's novel is accepted, dedicated to two women who refused to stay invisible, and the lighthouse light sweeps over the restaurant's opening night. His father, quietly, is in the last booth. Emotional beat: peace earned, love kept.
